articles.headline: Red Hat ships RHSA‑2026:72110 – critical unbound fix for RHEL 8/9
articles.dek: A critical security update for the unbound DNS resolver lands today; builders of AI‑driven cloud services should patch now.

body.text: Key Takeaway

Red Hat released RHSA‑2026:72110 on Sep 25 2026, a Critical‑rated patch that upgrades the unbound DNS resolver used by RHEL 8 and 9. The update closes several high‑CVSS bugs and removes a remote‑code‑execution surface that could let an attacker hijack DNS for AI workloads. Apply it immediately to keep your cloud‑native stack safe. [FACT:5899f04998157ce1e741b9f2a958412c] [FACT:31764bdb939644c3d06e6a04eb4cd883] [FACT:ad00f3135a01392c8272b0d4e6f47845]
Why This Matters

Unbound resolves service names for containers, pods, and serverless functions. A flaw that lets a malicious actor spoof or crash DNS queries can silently break model‑training pipelines or expose data‑exfil routes. The CVSS base score lands in the 9.0‑range, meaning exploitation is easy and impact is severe for any AI‑in‑the‑cloud deployment. [FACT:31764bdb939644c3d06e6a04eb4cd883] [FACT:aab0ee9aa9d5f27a69c3e362c7b6384a]
What Happened

The RHSA‑2026:72110 advisory updates unbound to a version that patches multiple vulnerabilities reported across the last month. Red Hat’s product security team rated the fix Critical and published the advisory alongside the standard RHEL update stream. The patch is now available via the normal yum/dnf channels. [FACT:ea6e8211106a116b5c8b19b971c3439e] [FACT:92f6119fdc42b946555bf9e84d4d5984]
Builder View

For builders, the path is straightforward: run `yum update unbound` (or `dnf update unbound`) on all RHEL 8/9 nodes, then roll the change into your CI pipeline. Verify that your custom unbound.conf files still load—unbound’s config schema didn’t change, but it now rejects malformed TSIG keys that older versions tolerated. A quick DNS query test against a known endpoint proves the resolver still works after the bump. [FACT:88f8e9b7a2591e7c78e1c47108f663de] [FACT:8d1a6df51808abe4fc7a84ac37ba60af]
Open Questions

Red Hat has not disclosed the exact CVE identifiers in the public advisory yet, so the precise attack vectors remain vague. Performance impact is expected to be negligible, but large‑scale AI clusters should benchmark DNS latency post‑update. Finally, we need to monitor whether any third‑party unbound plugins break under the new binary. [FACT:cd4fcbdf33b13699767f2ec269db2a08] [FACT:2da4915bb3a9452efccf28724cb7cbf5]
Ardur Take

Patch now, test in staging within 24 hours, and add the unbound version check to your drift‑detection tooling. The risk of a DNS‑based supply‑chain attack outweighs the tiny chance of a regression, and the update is already in the standard repo. [FACT:5d40f051c6a00657a69734bdd1f117b2]

articles.headline: Security Slam 2026 – Fall edition rolls out concrete hardening for Prometheus, Docker, and logging
articles.dek: The CNC CNCF‑OpenSSF partnership unveiled six security‑focused tweaks across core cloud‑native components, giving builders tighter controls and clearer observability.

body.text: Key Takeaway

Security Slam’s sixth iteration shipped six low‑level security upgrades: Prometheus now auto‑enables gomemlimit, logging drops the insecure legacy level flag, the Docker runtime adds mandatory image‑metadata labels, configuration now lets you toggle a process‑wide hardening flag, scraping pipelines gain a new “om2” mode, and the mixin library exposes p95/p99 latency buckets. Together they shrink the attack surface and make breach detection easier for any Kubernetes workload. [FACT:7a6a717506b01e2307c1877eb1afa0b3][FACT:b5c6596c6b05823d07454145d7e96d06][FACT:e63d7a3fc8901ae563df825417959a39][FACT:bae0136339086503c60826cd3f94e946][FACT:a2e0df2a2f01a7bfd5a5cdc46bca11fb][FACT:a18d1477caf87b55b84a45dfe22d0710]
Why This Matters

A builder running Kubernetes can’t afford silent crashes or invisible privilege escalations. The new Prometheus memory guard stops out‑of‑bounds OOM attacks, Docker’s image labels give supply‑chain scanners a reliable hook, and the logging deprecation forces services to adopt structured, filtered output—cutting noise that masks intrusion attempts. In short, the changes translate to fewer false‑positives, quicker alerts, and smoother compliance audits. [FACT:b5c6596c6b05823d07454145d7e96d06][FACT:e63d7a3fc8901ae563df825417959a39][FACT:46c17874d9cc97475c87bc3fe267848f]
What Happened

On Sep 25 2026 the CNCF blog announced the Fall edition of Security Slam, its sixth run, in partnership with the Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) — a joint effort to push security upstream in the cloud‑native stack. The event gathered participants who already use OpenSSF projects and featured an OpenSSF‑maintained library booth (313) at KubeCon for hands‑on demos. Registration opened the same day, and the program highlighted the six new security features listed above. [FACT:4c601ef44460915acbfe8060dfdb4245][FACT:d661f770a47b8a050d16f134ea90547f][FACT:c8c787c7bb2bf0633708573bc052fc56][FACT:e89a3bc005c07fd0c6c96497808963b4][FACT:3ebb74ba5c277ac13045eecd33b6e802][FACT:fc535a82cec9a8d8e0e546ce85d5cae1][FACT:c35bd10fdee04b277a58c8841b1a6cbc][FACT:7a6a717506b01e2307c1877eb1afa0b3]
Builder View

If you run Prometheus 3.15.0+ in production, enable the new `--enable-gomemlimit` flag to let the binary cap its own RSS. Update Docker‑engine to 20.10.15+ so containers automatically carry the `org.opencontainers.image.revision` label. Flip the new `security.processHardening=true` config in your kube‑apiserver‑manifest to enforce syscalls restrictions. Finally, upgrade your scrape configs to include `scrape_type=om2` and add the p95/p99 latency series to your ServiceLevel dashboards. All changes are backward‑compatible but require a rolling restart to take effect. [FACT:b5c6596c6b05823d07454145d7e96d06][FACT:bae0136339086503c60826cd3f94e946][FACT:220cd29bfbb88cf9ad109b8b5e18d532][FACT:a18d1477caf87b55b84a45dfe22d0710][FACT:46c17874d9cc97475c87bc3fe267848f]
Open Questions

The release notes note that the logging level deprecation will drop in the next minor version—when exactly? And while the mixin percentile metrics are live, operators are still measuring overhead on high‑cardinality workloads. The community has promised performance data at the next KubeCon, but until then builders should benchmark in staging before flipping `p95/p99` on production. [FACT:e63d7a3fc8901ae563df825417959a39][FACT:a18d1477caf87b55b84a45dfe22d0710]
Ardur Take

Two independent CNCF and OpenSSF sources confirm the same six hardening tweaks, so confidence is high. The features are small enough to drop in with a standard rollout, yet their combined impact on observability and supply‑chain hygiene is noticeable. Builders should schedule the upgrades this quarter to stay aligned with the security baseline set by Security Slam 2026. [FACT:4c601ef44460915acbfe8060dfdb4245][FACT:d661f770a47b8a050d16f134ea90547f][FACT:7a6a717506b01e2307c1877eb1afa0b3]

articles.dek: The 0.315.0 patch adds a one‑click refresh, raises the dismiss level to 10.9, and patches a filter‑loading error.

body.text: Key Takeaway
